_comment: Always-on agent instruction plane (BI-0020D511). The ratchet (scripts/check-instruction-plane-size.mjs) sums BYTES across `alwaysOn` plus every `alwaysOnExtracted` group, and forbids growth past scripts/instruction-plane-baseline.txt; the `pointerFile` may only force files listed in `alwaysOn` (closure check). Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-24-agent-instruction-plane-split-and-ratchet-design.md §4c (pointer-forced tier) and §12 (harness-injected tier).
_alwaysOnExtractedComment: The second always-on tier: content the HARNESS injects rather than the pointer forcing. Claude Code and Codex load every installed skill's frontmatter name+description into the system prompt of EVERY session; the bodies stay progressive-disclosure. Without this tier the Phase 1 split could shrink AGENTS.md by relocating prose into skill descriptions and the ratchet would report a win that never happened.
_ruleDestinationsComment: Where a rule is allowed to LIVE after Phase 1 relocates it out of always-on prose. scripts/check-instruction-plane-rule-coverage.mjs treats a baselined rule anchor as preserved if it is referenced from an always-on file OR from any file matched here; a rule referenced from neither was dropped, not moved, and fails. Widen this list when the split opens a new destination — that is a deliberate, reviewable act, which is the point.
_contentAssertionsComment: Source files that READ an always-on doc and assert on its CONTENT. These pin rules the anchor-based coverage check cannot see: Phase 1 relocated the principle_decide cost-axis sign rule and only dimension-catalog.test.ts caught it. Registered so whoever relocates doctrine next knows which tests to run; check-instruction-plane-rule-coverage.mjs reports any reader missing from this list so the set cannot grow silently.
_maxExtractedItemCharsComment: Per-skill budget for the serialised name+description BYTES the harness injects every session. Recalibrated 700 -> 300 by BI-58F6755A (model-era curation, DI-F844365B0DCC contingency marker). 700 permitted ~90-word descriptions that TAUGHT the skill; the body already teaches, on invoke. A description routes and nothing else. 300 leaves headroom above the widest legitimate trigger net (dpf-ux-fit-review, 257b) while forbidding a return to teaching descriptions.
_extractedItemStrictComment: Makes the per-description budget a HARD failure without waiting on structuralStrict, which stays false until the Phase 1 AGENTS.md split lands. Skill descriptions are already separate files, so their budget is not blocked by that split. Without this the aggregate ratchet alone would let one description balloon while others shrink. BI-58F6755A.
_maxDescriptionCharsComment: HARD platform limit, not a DPF budget: the Agent Skills API rejects a SKILL.md `description` over 1024 characters. Distinct from maxExtractedItemChars, which budgets the serialised name+description BYTES the harness injects. This one always errors (never advisory) because exceeding it is an install-time validation failure. Do not raise it — it is not ours to set.
